state.context: Can I32 handlers return opaque http::server_response with emits []. Every Can function needs mandatory assertions, but staged runs prove handler rows always fail with outcome mismatch: response constructors mint fresh tokens and the runner compares completions by identity plus deep equality, so actual and expected responses are never equal. The C contract excludes opaque values from assertion comparison and P10 defines responses as write-only sinks with no accessors, so no Can code can observe response content. Fixture paths still verify which boundary calls a handler made with which arguments, and staged loopback verifies wire status codes and bodies. P13 calls for supplied-completion callback assertions. HTML precedent never compares opaque success values; failures and void are compared instead.

opaque.instructions: Which design gives handlers honest passing assertions without breaking response opacity?

criteria.bare_opaque_ok: Allow bare ok in assertion expectations only, and only for excluded opaque results; the runner passes undefined-expected against opaque actuals. Rows still verify fixture structure, boundary-call arguments, and completion kinds; staged loopback verifies response content.
criteria.exempt_handlers: Exempt mounted-handler-shaped functions from mandatory assertions by design correction; staged loopback supplies all execution evidence and Can assertions cover models, mounts, and constructors.
criteria.vacuous_runner: Change the runner to pass every opaque-ok versus opaque-ok pair, reading the C exclusion as skipping comparison for all opaque types everywhere.
criteria.structural_response_compare: Keep valued expectations and teach the runner to compare responses structurally by reading status, headers, and body storage.
